verdicts.why: Names a room by how it is entered; no attitude toward it.
A formal gathering or ceremony, named plainly; the word takes no side on it.
An event at a critical time is a description of timing, not a judgement of the event.
The plainest verb for something coming about; whether it is welcome or not comes from context, not the word.
Chancing upon something says only that it was unplanned, with no attitude toward what was met.
An appointment with a doctor or lawyer is a plain label for a plain arrangement.
An official inspection visit is named neutrally; the word neither approves nor resents it.
The people of a nation, named collectively without judgement.
A region of indefinite boundary; the provincial sneer in 'country attorney' belongs to a different sense, not this gloss.

Against plain 'die', 'lost her father' is a softening that frames the death as the survivor's deprivation and signals tenderness and tact; I cannot settle whether that gentleness is a judgement of the person or simply the sense's meaning.
Letting something slip from sight or mind is described without blame or approval.
Failing to obtain something is an unwelcome outcome, but the word reports it plainly (bad referent, not loaded word).
Failing to catch a sound or a point is stated neutrally, with no contempt for the one who missed it.
Losing oneself in a book or in thought is a neutral description of absorption.
Making a loss in business is the plain accounting term; the referent is bad, the word is not.
Being set at a disadvantage is reported, not judged; there is no gentler or harsher plain neighbour it is chosen over.
A sorting operation is a technical description with no attitude attached.
One's manner of walking, named without approval or mockery (unlike 'swagger' or 'shuffle').
'Walk of life' groups careers without ranking them.
A horse's slowest gait is a technical term; slowness here is meaning, not attitude.
A baseball walk is a rule-defined event, described without judgement of batter or pitcher.
The distance between two places is a measurement; no attitude toward the gap.
A length of rope or pipe is a plain count-noun for a piece; nothing is judged.
Opening a meeting or speech is a neutral term for beginning it.
Unfolding or spreading something out is a physical action described without attitude.
Making something available is stated plainly; no approval is built into the word.
Becoming available (a position opening up) is neutral reportage.
A room opening onto a garden describes layout, not opinion.
Opening a file on a computer is a bare technical action.
Making the opening move in a game is a neutral term for going first.
